newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BANK BOS SEES ISSUE PRICE CLOSE TO PLN 29.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BANK BOS SEES ISSUE PRICE CLOSE TO PLN 29.

text.p: Polish Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS), whose public offering starts on Monday, will likely set its issue price close to the upper limit of the earlier set range of between 23 and 29 zlotys, BOS's deputy president said.
Jerzy Pietrewicz told Reuters on Friday that book-building showed high demand for the issue's 1.2 million shares.
"There's a lot of interest, much more than we expected, so the issue price will certainly be set at the highest or close to the highest level of the range," he said.
The final issue price will be announced on Saturday.
Pietrewicz said that BOS, which seeks a main-market listing in January 1997, had given up the idea of underwriting the issue because of the large demand.
Large investors can register for at least 25,000 shares in the large-investor tranche of 800,000 shares, while 400,000 shares are being offered in the small-investor tranche.
Pietrewicz also said the bank had not ruled out a new share issue in 1997.

"We're not ruling out a new share issue, but not earlier than in the second half of next year, but we must ensure that the amount and the time of the offer would not dilute the firm's earnings per share," he said.
BOS, which specialises in funding environmental protection projects, had a net profit of 31.8 million zlotys in 1995 on 210.6 million zlotys in interest and other related revenues.

The bank's main shareholders are the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management, with 44.4 percent, the State Treasury, with 7.8 percent, and Ciech SA with 5.8 percent. -- Malgorzata Rzepka +48 22 653 9700
